ship_by_class.meaning: Adds a ship line that is filled from a class of NPC ships. Value 0 minimum count, value 1 maximum count (both read unconditionally, a missing one is 0), value 2 class id: either the nickname of a `[ShipClass]` in `missions\shipclasses.ini` (an NPC ship archetype fits if one of that class's `member` ids is in its `npc_class` list) or directly an `npc_class` word of an archetype (or a mission property of its ship in `shiparch.ini`); see random-missions.md, value 3 optional difficulty offset (0 if absent). When the encounter is bound to a zone with level L the class `diff<N>` is added to the line, with `N = max(1, L + offset)`; an archetype fits a line only if it satisfies **every** class of the line, so archetypes are expected to carry the matching `diff<N>` word in their `npc_class`.

Values 1-5 are integers consumed by the loot generator (SpaceSupport.cpp:413): value 1 a minimum worth (sum of the players' worth) below which nothing drops, value 2 the divisor applied to the excess worth (0 keeps the item count), value 3 a base amount added to the scaled amount, value 4 a cap on that sum (which is also limited by the carried item count), value 5 a cap on the final count after the chance has been applied. These meanings are inferred from the consumer's arithmetic; the port has no names for them.

generic_priority.meaning: Priority used for generic (non-specific) effects of the type.  ‖  Upper level up to which the `vis_generic` variant is used instead (see `vis_generic`).

lod_type.meaning: `EFT_LOD_TRAIL`, `EFT_LOD_WEAPON`, `EFT_LOD_SMALL`, `EFT_LOD_MEDIUM`, `EFT_LOD_LARGE`, `EFT_LOD_SMALL_DISTANT` (case-insensitive). Selects the row of `[EffectLOD]` used for distance fading.  ‖  `EFT_LOD_TRAIL`, `EFT_LOD_WEAPON`, `EFT_LOD_SMALL`, `EFT_LOD_MEDIUM`, `EFT_LOD_LARGE` or `EFT_LOD_SMALL_DISTANT` (case-insensitive). `EFT_LOD_NONE` is not accepted; any other text leaves the value unchanged without a message.

radius.heading: 4.1 `[EffectType]`

visibility.meaning: `EXIST_OFFSCREEN` keeps the effect alive off screen; any other word sets the flag off.  ‖  `EXIST_OFFSCREEN` (case-insensitive) = the effect exists off screen; any other text = it does not.
visibility.heading: 4.1 `[EffectType]`

update.meaning: `UPDATE_OFFSCREEN` keeps updating off screen; any other word sets the flag off.  ‖  `UPDATE_OFFSCREEN` (case-insensitive) = updated off screen; any other text = not.
update.heading: 4.1 `[EffectType]`

run_time.meaning: Run time in seconds; table entries use `-1` for continuous effects (a negative value sets a flag on the effect archetype, see effect_type_info.h).  ‖  Run time in seconds; a negative value marks a continuous effect.
run_time.heading: 4.1 `[EffectType]`

fps.meaning: Update rate of the effect.  ‖  Update rate.
fps.heading: 4.1 `[EffectType]`

pbubble.meaning: Near and far distance of the effect's "pbubble" range. A warning `pbubble ranges backwards` is logged when far < near (the values are still stored).  ‖  Visibility distance bubble: the working distance is interpolated from the first value (full effects detail) to the second (lowest detail) by the effects performance setting. Far below near logs the warning "pbubble ranges backwards" but is kept.

type.meaning: Row to define: `lod_type_trail`, `lod_type_weapon`, `lod_type_small`, `lod_type_medium`, `lod_type_large`, `lod_type_small_distant` (case-insensitive). `none` is not accepted. Between `min_lod_screen_size` and this value the blend rises linearly.
max_lod_screen_size.heading: 4.2 `[EffectLOD]`

min_lod_screen_size.meaning: Screen size at which the fade-in starts (blend = `(size - min_lod) / (max_lod - min_lod)`, clamped to `0 ... 1`).  ‖  On-screen size at which the LOD blend is 0.

min_screen_size.meaning: Effects smaller than this on screen are not drawn at all.  ‖  On-screen size at or below which the effect is not drawn at all.
min_screen_size.heading: 4.2 `[EffectLOD]`

file.meaning: Texture archive (`.txm`) to load; the path goes to the data file system. An empty value, or the same name as the previous `file` (case-insensitive), is ignored. If the archive cannot be opened the game logs `file not found`. All archives loaded by one call are released again at the end of the load, so the textures stay only as long as shapes reference them. Resets the current texture.

name.meaning: Selects the texture by name inside the loaded archives (CRC-32 of the name). A texture that is not found logs `missing texture`; the current texture is then empty. Logs `shape definition never followed texture` if the previous texture selection was not followed by a shape.
name.heading: 5.1 `[Texture]` section (repeated)

texture_name.meaning: Selects the texture by name inside the loaded archives (CRC-32 of the name). A texture that is not found logs `missing texture`; the current texture is then empty. Logs `shape definition never followed texture` if the previous texture selection was not followed by a shape.
texture_name.heading: 5.1 `[Texture]` section (repeated)

tex_shape.meaning: Shortcut: selects the texture of that name **and** creates a shape of the same name covering the whole texture. A missing texture is skipped.

dim.meaning: `dim = x, y, w, h [, ul_u, ul_v, lr_u, lr_v]` — sets the rectangle of the shape just started by `shape_name` (see 5.3). The first four values are required; the last four read as `0` when omitted. A `dim` without a preceding `shape_name` logs an error and is ignored; it ends the shape (a second `dim` needs a new `shape_name`).
dim.heading: 5.1 `[Texture]` section (repeated)

name.meaning: Shape name. A section without a name logs `no shape name was specified`.

Kind and severity are parsed as numbers, so `65540`, `'I'` and `0x10004` are all accepted.  ‖  Repeatable `log = where[, kind[, severity]]`, one log channel per line (channels are pushed to the front of the list, except `$Window` channels, which are appended). `[0]` where: `$Text` (debugger output), `$Window` (message box, case-insensitive match on the `$` names) or any other text = file name, opened with `"wb"` (truncated). Longer than 127 characters is cut. `[1]` kind, default -1 (all kinds): a number or a quoted character such as `'c'` (character literals are accepted by the number parser); it is compared with the message flags shifted right by 4. `[2]` severity limit, default 100: messages whose severity (the low nibble of the message flags; 1 = error, 2 = warning, 3 = notice in the flags the code uses) is numerically above the limit are dropped. act_spawnshiprel.type: str (47); id; str (47); str; float; float; str
act_spawnshiprel.meaning: Spawns one ship placed relative to the reference object. Mode: `POINT` (0), `DIRECTIONAL` (1), `RELATIVE` (2); other words leave -1. Offset is a vector in the reference frame; a heading >= 0 (degrees, pi/180 applied) yields a rotated frame. With value 8 the spawned ship gets that new nickname. Value 1 `no_ol` keeps the ship's own objectives.
act_spawnshiprel.heading: Spawning, removing and moving objects

act_spawnsolar.meaning: Spawns the named solar. Value 1 non-empty overrides the position (needs 1,2,3), value 4 non-empty the orientation (otherwise the solar's own).
act_spawnsolar.heading: Spawning, removing and moving objects

act_spawnformation.meaning: Spawns the whole group; the optional values override the group's position/orientation.
act_spawnformation.heading: Spawning, removing and moving objects

act_spawnloot.meaning: Spawns the loot crate; optional position/orientation override.
act_spawnloot.heading: Spawning, removing and moving objects

act_destroy.meaning: Destroys the object with that label: `EXPLODE` (1) or `SILENT` (0).
act_destroy.heading: Spawning, removing and moving objects

act_relocateship.meaning: Teleports the object to the position (and orientation) in the player's current system.
act_relocateship.heading: Spawning, removing and moving objects

act_relocateform.meaning: Moves the NPC's whole formation: each member is placed at its formation slot relative to the given frame.
act_relocateform.heading: Spawning, removing and moving objects

act_setorient.meaning: Rotates the object in place (position unchanged). The quaternion is stored as given (no normalisation in the parser) and converted to a matrix when the action runs.
act_setorient.heading: Spawning, removing and moving objects

act_moveplayer.meaning: If the player's ship is farther than the radius from the point, teleports it to the point (keeping its orientation); otherwise nothing happens. Needs the player in space.
act_moveplayer.heading: Spawning, removing and moving objects

act_setinitialplayerpos.meaning: Sets the position and orientation the player will launch with.
act_setinitialplayerpos.heading: Spawning, removing and moving objects

act_removecargo.meaning: Removes that many units of the loot's equipment from the player's cargo.
act_removecargo.heading: Spawning, removing and moving objects

act_lightfuse.meaning: Lights a fuse (`fuses.ini`) on the object.
act_lightfuse.heading: Spawning, removing and moving objects

act_disabletradelane.meaning: Drains the ring's shields (disables the lane).
act_disabletradelane.heading: Spawning, removing and moving objects

act_lockdock.meaning: Locks or unlocks docking at a gate/hole. Target is `Player` or `Everyone` (case-sensitive); other values do nothing. Mode `lock` or `unlock`.
act_lockdock.heading: Spawning, removing and moving objects

act_jumper.meaning: Marks every NPC with the label as a gate-jumper (or clears the flag).
act_jumper.heading: Spawning, removing and moving objects

act_setlifetime.meaning: Sets the NPC's remaining lifetime (a named NPC, else every NPC carrying the label).
act_setlifetime.heading: Spawning, removing and moving objects

act_invulnerable.meaning: Makes the object(s) invulnerable (`pub::SpaceObj::SetInvincible`); the state is remembered for saves. Meaning of the second flag is passed straight to the engine.
act_invulnerable.heading: Spawning, removing and moving objects

act_adjhealth.meaning: Adds `delta` to the relative health (0..1) of every object with the label, clamped to [0, 1].
act_adjhealth.heading: Spawning, removing and moving objects

act_cloak.meaning: Activates (`true`) / deactivates (`false`) the cloak equipment on every object with the label; decloaked names are remembered for saves.
act_cloak.heading: Spawning, removing and moving objects

act_setshipandloadout.meaning: Changes the player's ship archetype and loadout (`pub::GetShipID` / `pub::GetLoadoutID`; `none` skips that part). A loadout name is resolved only if value 1 is present.
act_setshipandloadout.heading: Spawning, removing and moving objects

act_forceland.meaning: Forces the player to land at the base.
act_forceland.heading: Spawning, removing and moving objects

act_dockrequest.meaning: Orders the first player's ship to dock with the object.
act_dockrequest.heading: Spawning, removing and moving objects

act_adjacct.meaning: Adds (or subtracts) cash from the player's account.
act_adjacct.heading: Spawning, removing and moving objects

act_giveobjlist.meaning: Gives the NPC the directive list (it loses its guide).
act_giveobjlist.heading: NPC behavior, formations and vibes

act_givemb.meaning: Gives the NPC the first guide of the list.
act_givemb.heading: NPC behavior, formations and vibes

act_pobjidle.meaning: Sends an idle directive to the player's ship.
act_pobjidle.heading: NPC behavior, formations and vibes

act_playerform.meaning: Forms the player and the NPC into the formation from `formations.ini`.
act_playerform.heading: NPC behavior, formations and vibes

act_setpriority.meaning: `NORMAL` -> 1, `ALWAYS_EXECUTE` -> 0, other words 0; applied to NPCs with the label.
act_setpriority.heading: NPC behavior, formations and vibes

act_pilotparams.meaning: `no_flee` -> 0, `normal_flee` -> 1; other words keep 0. Mode 0 forces the NPC's flee parameters to the "never flee" set; mode 1 re-reads them from its pilot personality.
act_pilotparams.heading: NPC behavior, formations and vibes

act_setflee.meaning: Mode `CLEAR` (2), `SET_POS` (0), `SET_OBJ` (1). Sets or clears the NPC's flee destination. The bool is passed to the engine as-is (SET_OBJ).
act_setflee.heading: NPC behavior, formations and vibes

act_setvibe.meaning: Sets the attitude of object A towards B. Value 2 is the lower bound, value 3 (when present) the upper bound of the range; with only value 2 both are equal. A value is a number when its first character is a digit or `-`; otherwise it must be one of the `REP_*` words (see below), unknown words give -2.0.
act_setvibe.heading: NPC behavior, formations and vibes

act_setvibelbltoship.meaning: Attitude of each member of a label group towards a ship.
act_setvibelbltoship.heading: NPC behavior, formations and vibes

act_setvibeshiptolbl.meaning: Attitude of a ship towards each member of a label group.
act_setvibeshiptolbl.heading: NPC behavior, formations and vibes

act_setvibeofferbasehack.meaning: Sets the player's reputation towards the base's faction to 1.0 (a hack used by offer missions).
act_setvibeofferbasehack.heading: NPC behavior, formations and vibes

act_setrep.meaning: Sets the reputation of the object (or the player) with the faction. Value 2 is a number when the engine's `is_number` accepts it; otherwise it is looked up in the `REP_*` words below (unknown -> -2.0).
act_setrep.heading: NPC behavior, formations and vibes

act_enableenc.meaning: Resets and enables that random encounter.
act_enableenc.heading: NPC behavior, formations and vibes

act_disablefriendlyfire.meaning: Adds each label to the mission's list of "friendly fire excused" labels (saved in `[MissionState]`). Reads values until the first empty one.
act_disablefriendlyfire.heading: NPC behavior, formations and vibes

act_lockmaneuvers.meaning: Locks (`true`) or unlocks the player's manoeuvres.
act_lockmaneuvers.heading: NPC behavior, formations and vibes

act_enablemaneuver.meaning: Enables or disables one manoeuvre of the player (name via `BehaviorTypes::get_behavior_id`; unknown names are not validated).
act_enablemaneuver.heading: NPC behavior, formations and vibes

act_playerenemyclamp.meaning: Passed to `pub::AI::set_player_enemy_clamp` for the player's ship.
act_playerenemyclamp.heading: NPC behavior, formations and vibes

act_playercandock.meaning: Enables docking for the player; the listed objects are exceptions (inverse of the flag).
act_playercandock.heading: NPC behavior, formations and vibes

act_playercantradelane.meaning: Enables trade lanes for the player; each listed pair (ring A, ring B) is an exception. Pairs are read two values at a time.
act_playercantradelane.heading: NPC behavior, formations and vibes

act_naggreet.meaning: Greeting nag: when the player's ship finishes launching, the speaker plays `nag_greet_combat` or `nag_greet_normal` (by its combat state). A nag id that already exists is kept (the new one is dropped). The speaker's voice/costume come from its `[NPC]` record.
act_naggreet.heading: Nag actions

act_nagdistleaving.type: id; str (47); str (47); int; float; str
act_nagdistleaving.meaning: Nag when the player is leaving the area. With the target `position` (or an empty target) the speaker is dropped and the generic line `nag_leaving_mission_area` is used; `position` takes a fixed point from values 3..5. A distance value of exactly -1 is replaced by 4000.0. Combat mode (case-insensitive): `NAG_IN_COMBAT` (only while the target ship is in combat), `NAG_OUT_OF_COMBAT`, `NAG_ALWAYS`; other words keep the default. An existing nag with the same id is replaced.
act_nagdistleaving.heading: Nag actions

act_nagdisttowards.type: str; id; str (47); str (47); int; float; str
act_nagdisttowards.meaning: Nag when the player is **not** approaching the target. In `OBJ` form the distance -1 becomes 4000.0; in `POS` form the distance is used as given. A value 0 other than `OBJ`/`POS` is treated as `POS`. An existing nag with the same id is replaced.
act_nagdisttowards.heading: Nag actions

act_nagclamp.meaning: Sets the mission's nag clamp (stops all nag processing) and a per-ship flag on every mission NPC (`FContentNpcShip::SetField1b1`; the NPC-side effect is not identified in the source).
act_nagclamp.heading: Nag actions

act_sendcomm.type: str (47); str (47); nick; int; str; int; str
act_sendcomm.meaning: Plays a comm from a ship in the player's system. Duration must be -1 or 1..10 (seconds); any other number (including 0) becomes -1, which means 0.5 s (1.0 s when the receiver is the player's ship). Values 4 onwards are only read when value 4 is present; value 6 `NO_HEAD` means no head part; a costume given here is registered with the mission when the receiver is `Player`.
act_sendcomm.heading: Comms and audio

act_ethercomm.type: str; int; str (47); nick; int; str
act_ethercomm.meaning: A comm that comes from nowhere (no sender ship). All values are read (none optional); the duration rule is as for `Act_SendComm`.
act_ethercomm.heading: Comms and audio

act_playsoundeffect.meaning: Plays a sound effect for the player.
act_playsoundeffect.heading: Comms and audio

act_playmusic.meaning: Sets the player's music (`pub::Audio::SetMusic`, a 4-id + float + flag record). A value that is empty or the word `none` leaves its slot unchanged. If value 0 is empty or the word `no_params` the music is cancelled instead (`pub::Audio::CancelMusic`). The roles of the four track slots, of the float and of the flag are not named in the source.
act_playmusic.heading: Comms and audio

act_addambient.meaning: Starts an ambient (background) bar scene in that room of the base; remembered in `[MissionState]`.
act_addambient.heading: Comms and audio

act_removeambient.meaning: Stops the scene started by `Act_AddAmbient` with that file name.
act_removeambient.heading: Comms and audio

act_addrtc.meaning: Starts a `[CharacterEncounter]` RTC script (see missions-support.md). Only the exact word `repeatable` (case-insensitive) matters. Remembered in `[MissionState] rtc =`.
act_addrtc.heading: Comms and audio

act_removertc.meaning: Marks the started script with that path as finished and releases its character.
act_removertc.heading: Comms and audio

act_callthorn.meaning: Runs a Thorn (cutscene) script (`pub::SpaceObj::RequestSpaceScript`). If value 2 is empty: value 1 is the target (default `Player`), mode 1. Otherwise the target is `Player`, values 1..3 are an integer position, mode 2. Also locks out the player (invulnerable, NPC and GCS clamps on) until `Act_RevertCam`.
act_callthorn.heading: Comms and audio

act_staticcam.meaning: Switches the player to a fixed camera (and invulnerable, NPC and GCS clamps on) until `Act_RevertCam`.
act_staticcam.heading: Comms and audio

act_revertcam.meaning: Returns the camera to the player and removes the clamps set by `Act_StaticCam` / `Act_CallThorn`.
act_revertcam.heading: Comms and audio

act_randompop.meaning: Enables (`true`) or disables random NPC population.
act_randompop.heading: Random population and space clamps

act_randompopsphere.meaning: `off` adds a sphere in which no random population spawns; `on` removes such a sphere. Any other word keeps `on`.
act_randompopsphere.heading: Random population and space clamps

act_rpoptlattacksenabled.meaning: Enables random attacks in trade lanes.
act_rpoptlattacksenabled.heading: Random population and space clamps

act_gcsclamp.meaning: Sets the generic communication system (GCS) clamp.
act_gcsclamp.heading: Random population and space clamps

act_hostileclamp.meaning: The value is **inverted** when stored (`true` stores 0, `false` stores 1) and passed to the population manager's hostile clamp.
act_hostileclamp.heading: Random population and space clamps

cnd_timer.meaning: Fires after the accumulated heartbeat time reaches the duration. With value 1 present the duration is drawn **once at load** uniformly from [value 0, value 1] with `rand()`. Mode `RUN_ON_BASE` counts also while the player is docked; `RUN_IN_SPACE_ONLY` counts only while the player has a ship; other words keep the default. Fails if the mission has no player. Save line: `Cnd_Timer = <elapsed seconds>`. Wakes on heartbeat.
cnd_timer.heading: Conditions

cnd_baseenter.meaning: Player-side base entry event. `ANY` is a **case-sensitive** compare (`any` would be looked up as a base name). The event's base id must equal the value, unless it is unset. Wakes on `BaseEnter`.
cnd_baseenter.heading: Conditions

cnd_baseexit.meaning: As `Cnd_BaseEnter`, for leaving a base. Wakes on `BaseExit`.
cnd_baseexit.heading: Conditions

cnd_locenter.meaning: Player enters a room of that base (`pub::GF::FindLocation(base, room)`); the player's current base must be that base and the event location must match. Wakes on `LocationEnter`.
cnd_locenter.heading: Conditions

cnd_locexit.meaning: As `Cnd_LocEnter`, leaving the room. Wakes on `LocationExit`.
cnd_locexit.heading: Conditions

cnd_charselect.meaning: The player clicks the named bar/room character while in that room. The role name is matched against the characters of the room (e.g. RTC `actor` roles). Wakes on `GFObjSelect`.
cnd_charselect.heading: Conditions

cnd_rumorheard.meaning: The player hears the named rumor in that room (name compared case-insensitively with the event's name). Parsed exactly like `Cnd_CharSelect`. Wakes on `RumorHeard`.
cnd_rumorheard.heading: Conditions

cnd_spaceenter.meaning: Player enters space (launch/undock) in that system. Value 0 absent or exactly `no_params` (case-sensitive) = any system. Wakes on `SpaceEnter`.
cnd_spaceenter.heading: Conditions

cnd_spaceexit.meaning: Player leaves space (docks). Same grammar. Wakes on `SpaceExit`.
cnd_spaceexit.heading: Conditions

cnd_systementer.meaning: Player enters a system, optionally coming from another one (`ANY` is case-insensitive here). On activation (no event) it is true when the player is already in that system. Wakes on `SystemEnter`.
cnd_systementer.heading: Conditions

cnd_systemexit.meaning: Player leaves a system (optionally towards a given system). Wakes on `SystemExit`.
cnd_systemexit.heading: Conditions

cnd_jumpincomplete.meaning: The player finished a jump into that system. The event's ship must be the player's ship. Wakes on `JumpInComplete`.
cnd_jumpincomplete.heading: Conditions

cnd_jumpgateact.meaning: A jump gate with that nickname was activated. Wakes on `JumpgateAct`.
cnd_jumpgateact.heading: Conditions

cnd_launchcomplete.meaning: The labelled ship finished launching from a base (optionally that base). Wakes on `LaunchComplete`.
cnd_launchcomplete.heading: Conditions

cnd_playerlaunch.meaning: The mission's player launched. Wakes on `PlayerLaunch`.
cnd_playerlaunch.heading: Conditions

cnd_inspace.meaning: True when the player has a ship object (in space); `false` = docked. Polled.
cnd_inspace.heading: Conditions

cnd_hasmsn.meaning: True when the player does (`yes`) / does not (`no`) currently have a live mission. The compare is **case-sensitive**; other words leave `yes`. Polled.
cnd_hasmsn.heading: Conditions

cnd_destroyed.meaning: An object carrying the label was destroyed. Count: values < -1 are ignored (stay -1); -1 = true when at most one object of the label is still in the mission's label table; N >= 0 counts matching destroy events and fires when the counter equals N (so 0 never fires). Kind: `EXPLODE` (1), `SILENT` (0), `ALL` (any kind), `ALL_IGNORE_LANDING` (any kind, but only while the player has a ship); other words keep the default. A killer label restricts who destroyed it. Save line: `Cnd_Destroyed = <count>`. Wakes on `ObjectDestroyed`.
cnd_destroyed.heading: Conditions

cnd_healthdec.meaning: The object's relative health (0..1) dropped to or below the fraction, optionally damaged by the attacker. On activation (no event) only checks the player's own state when no attacker label is given. Wakes on `ObjectDamaged`.
cnd_healthdec.heading: Conditions

cnd_projhit.meaning: The target was hit by projectiles `needed` times (counter >= needed). Save line: `Cnd_ProjHit = <count>`. Wakes on `ObjectDamaged`.
cnd_projhit.heading: Conditions

cnd_projhitshiptolbl.meaning: As `Cnd_ProjHit`, but the target is any object carrying the label (group). Save line: `Cnd_ProjHitShipToLbl = <count>`. Wakes on `ObjectDamaged`.
cnd_projhitshiptolbl.heading: Conditions

cnd_lootacquired.meaning: The labelled ship picked up loot carrying the loot label. With count -1 it fires when every loot object of that label has been picked up; otherwise when the counter equals the count. Save line: `Cnd_LootAcquired = <count>`. Wakes on `LootAcquired`.
cnd_lootacquired.heading: Conditions

cnd_cargoscanned.meaning: The scanner ship scanned the scanned ship's cargo. **Both values must be present**, otherwise the line is ignored. The word `none` (case-sensitive) means "unresolved/any". Wakes on `CargoScanned`.
cnd_cargoscanned.heading: Conditions

cnd_commcomplete.meaning: A comm with that text finished playing (optionally from the labelled ship). Wakes on `CommComplete`.
cnd_commcomplete.heading: Conditions

cnd_rtcdone.meaning: The RTC script started with that path (compared case-insensitively with the path given to `Act_AddRTC`) finished. Wakes on `RtcDone`.
cnd_rtcdone.heading: Conditions

cnd_msnresponse.meaning: The player's answer to the mission offer. Other words keep `accept`. Wakes on `MissionResponse`.
cnd_msnresponse.heading: Conditions

cnd_popupdialog.meaning: The player pressed this button of an `Act_PopUpDialog`: `YES` (1), `NO` (2), `LATER` (4), `CLOSE` (8). Other words leave mask 0. Wakes on `PopUpDialog`.
cnd_popupdialog.heading: Conditions

cnd_enclaunched.meaning: A random encounter with this id was launched. Wakes on `EncounterLaunched`.
cnd_enclaunched.heading: Conditions

cnd_intradelane.meaning: True when the object is (`true`) / is not (`false`) in a trade lane. Label `Player` (case-insensitive) = the player's ship, otherwise an NPC of the mission by name. Polled.
cnd_intradelane.heading: Conditions

cnd_tlentered.meaning: The ship entered the trade lane between these two rings (both must match). Wakes on `TradelaneEnter`.
cnd_tlentered.heading: Conditions

cnd_tlexited.meaning: The ship left a trade lane (unset ring = any). Note the event's two ring slots are compared the other way round to `Cnd_TLEntered`: value 1 against the event's third slot, value 2 against its second. Wakes on `TradelaneExit`.
cnd_tlexited.heading: Conditions

cnd_inzone.meaning: True when the object is (`true`) / is not (`false`) inside a zone of the given type: `OBJECT_ZONE` (0x7fc0), `EXCLUSION_ZONE` (0x30000), `NEBULA_ZONE` (0x8000), `DUST_ZONE` (0x200000). With no/unknown type the flags are 0, so `true` can never match and `false` always matches. Needs the player in space. Polled.
cnd_inzone.heading: Conditions

cnd_cmptoplane.meaning: Evaluates `A*x + B*y + C*z + D` for the object's position; `inside` matches when the value is below 0, `outside` when above 0 (zero matches neither). Needs the player in space. Polled.
cnd_cmptoplane.heading: Conditions

cnd_distship.type: str; str (47); str (47); float; float; str
cnd_distship.meaning: Distance between two objects (same system) compared with the distance (squared when > 0): `inside` = closer than, `outside` = farther than. The relation must hold for the hold time (value 4 is used only when > 0), which counts down on each heartbeat while the relation holds and resets when it does not. Tick mode: `TICK_ALWAYS` (0) counts always; `TICK_TOWARDS` (1) counts only while the distance is not growing; `TICK_AWAY` (2) only while it is not shrinking. Needs the player in space. Save line: `Cnd_DistShip = <timer>, <last distance squared>`. Polled.
cnd_distship.heading: Conditions

cnd_distvec.type: str; str (47); float; float; float; str
cnd_distvec.meaning: As `Cnd_DistShip` against a fixed point. The distance is squared unless it is <= 0; the hold time is used when >= 0. Save line: `Cnd_DistVec = <timer>, <last distance squared>`. Polled.
cnd_distvec.heading: Conditions

cnd_distveclbl.type: str; str; id; float; float; float
cnd_distveclbl.meaning: As `Cnd_DistVec` for every object carrying the label: value 1 equal to `any` (case-insensitive) walks the objects one by one (every in-range object decrements the shared timer, every out-of-range object reloads it) and fires as soon as the timer reaches 0; any other word requires all objects of the label to be in range at once before the timer counts down. Distance squared unless <= 0. Save line: `Cnd_DistVecLbl = <timer>`. Polled.
cnd_distveclbl.heading: Conditions

cnd_distcircle.meaning: True on the heartbeat in which the object's movement since the previous check crosses the plane of the circle defined by the solar object (plane normal from its orientation, radius from its bounding sphere), within that radius. Needs the player in space. Polled.
cnd_distcircle.heading: Conditions

cnd_tetherbroke.meaning: Tracks two ships. Time accumulates only after a `TetherObject` message for exactly these two ships reported the tether as released, and only while their squared distance is at least `distance` (squared when > 0); the condition fires when the accumulated time reaches `seconds`. The optional inner distance (value 4, squared unless negative; default 0 = unused) changes this: while the squared distance is below it, time accumulates only if the distance is not shrinking. Save line: `Cnd_TetherBroke = <accumulated>, <last distance>`. Wakes on `TetherObject`.
cnd_tetherbroke.heading: Conditions

cnd_npcsystementer.meaning: True when every listed NPC **and the player** have entered the system (a label listed as `Player` is dropped and the player appended implicitly). Waits 2 s after the awaited NPCs are created, or 10 s after the player arrives through a gate/hole. Labels that no longer resolve are forgotten unless NPCs from a loaded save are still awaited. At most 49 labels are read (index < 50). Save line (no newline): `Cnd_NPCSystemEnter = <label>,<system id>, <label>,<system id>, ...`. Wakes on `NpcSystemEnter`, `Heartbeat`, `NpcShipCreated`.
cnd_npcsystementer.heading: Conditions

cnd_npcsystemexit.meaning: As above for leaving; every label (including `Player`) is kept as written, nothing is appended. Save line `Cnd_NPCSystemExit = <label>,<system id>, ...`. Wakes on `NpcSystemExit`.
cnd_npcsystemexit.heading: Conditions

cnd_playermaneuver.meaning: The player ship is running that behavior (name -> `BehaviorTypes::get_behavior_id`; an unknown name is not validated). If the text of value 1 contains the substring `inverse` the result is negated (including all early-outs), and the text is also used as the target label. For the formation behavior the targeted NPC must share the player's formation. Wakes on `PlayerManeuver`.
cnd_playermaneuver.heading: Conditions

cnd_watchtrigger.meaning: True while the named trigger is in the given state: `ACTIVE`, `INACTIVE`, `COMPLETE`; `ON` = `ACTIVE`; `OFF` = `INACTIVE` or `COMPLETE`. Unknown trigger -> false. Polled.
cnd_watchtrigger.heading: Conditions

cnd_watchvibe.type: str (47); str (47); float or word; str
cnd_watchvibe.meaning: The attitude of A towards B compared with the value: `lt` (<=), `gt` (>=), `eq` (==); other words keep `lt`. Value 2 is a number when its first character is a digit or `-`; otherwise it must be one of `REP_HOSTILE_MAXIMUM` (-1.0), `REP_HOSTILE_THRESHOLD` (-0.6), `REP_NEUTRAL_HOSTILE` (-0.2), `REP_NEUTRAL` (0.0), `REP_NEUTRAL_FRIENDLY` (0.2), `REP_FRIEND_THRESHOLD` (0.6), `REP_FRIEND_MAXIMUM` (1.0); an unknown word silently becomes -2.0. Polled.
cnd_watchvibe.heading: Conditions

nickname.meaning: Trigger id used by `Act_ActTrig`, `Act_DeactTrig`, `Cnd_WatchTrigger`, `Act_Save`.  ‖  Evaluated with `MissionStateFromName` and the result discarded.
nickname.heading: `[Trigger]`

initstate.meaning: `ACTIVE`, `INACTIVE` or `COMPLETE` (case-insensitive); any other word leaves the state `INACTIVE`. Triggers that are `ACTIVE` at load are activated by the mission-start message.
initstate.heading: `[Trigger]`

repeatable.meaning: `true` re-arms the trigger after it fires; `false` has no effect.
repeatable.heading: `[Trigger]`

state.meaning: Evaluated with `MissionStateFromName` and the result discarded.
state.heading: `[Trigger]`

ship_bought.meaning: The player has bought a new ship (reputation hack flag).
ship_bought.heading: `[StoryInfo]`

mission.meaning: Name of the story mission controller to create on load: `Mission_01a`, `Mission_01b`, `Mission_02` .. `Mission_13`, `GenericMission`, or `No_Mission` (no mission). For `GenericMission` value 1 is the mission script path (see missions.md). **The writer emits only value 0**, so a saved `GenericMission` loses its path. The name is not validated; an unknown name creates no controller.
mission.heading: `[StoryInfo]`

missionnum.meaning: Current story stage (0..42; see stage names). Triggers sending the `PlayerLoad` and `MissionStart` messages to the story mission. Written only if a mission is active or the stage is not 0.
missionnum.heading: `[StoryInfo]`

delta_worth.meaning: Cash+asset worth needed before the next story mission starts (`-1` = none).
delta_worth.heading: `[StoryInfo]`

missionstatenum.meaning: The mission's state (`FAIL`/`SUCCEED`/`NO_STATE` codes). In `Mission_01a` it is written only after the player entered the first base and, on load, sets the current and previous state and re-sends objectives unless it is 3. In `Mission_01b` it is read after the script re-creates the post-acceptance state.
missionstatenum.heading: `[Mission01aSave]`, `[Mission01bSave]`

missionstatenum.meaning: The mission's state (`FAIL`/`SUCCEED`/`NO_STATE` codes). In `Mission_01a` it is written only after the player entered the first base and, on load, sets the current and previous state and re-sends objectives unless it is 3. In `Mission_01b` it is read after the script re-creates the post-acceptance state.
missionstatenum.heading: `[Mission01aSave]`, `[Mission01bSave]`

locked_gate.meaning: Registers a gate lock for this player (repeatable).

know.meaning: The NPC sells information. Dropped if `level >= 4` (unsigned). Offered while the feeling reaches the level and the player does not yet know the item (rumor id in value 1). Value 2 is the price; values 0 and 1 are string-table ids.

rumor.meaning: A rumor the NPC may tell between two story stages (names from stage names, case-insensitive). A stage name that is not in the table reuses the previous lookup result (value 0: an indeterminate value; value 1: the result of value 0). `level` is **not validated** (an index >= 4 reads outside the threshold table). At most 8 ids fit in the record, but the loop has no bound check. The record always loads. Weight: 0x40 for a rumor bounded on both ends (from stage > 0 and to stage < 42), else `(level + 1) * 5`.

docking_sphere.meaning: One docking sphere per line; repeated keys **append**. `[0]`: `berth` (1), `moor_small` (3), `moor_medium` (4), `moor_large` (5), `ring` (6), `pad` (6), `jump` (7), `airlock` (8), case-insensitive; any other name gives type 0 (no message). `[1]` is lower-cased on read. `[3]` is the dock animation script name (stored only if present).

fuse.meaning: Damage fuse for the whole object; repeated keys **append**. In `Server.dll` the fuse is lit (with `[1]` as its start time argument) when the object's hit points are at or below `[2]`, and when damage makes the hit points cross `[2]` (server_gameobject.cpp:1193, :1455); so `[2]` is the hit-point threshold and `[1]` the start time. The client reader names the two floats the other way round (client_equip_fx.cpp:3410); the two port modules disagree and this was not settled against the retail binary here. Fuse files: see server.md.

shield_link.type: `[0]` shield archetype (id), `[1]` shield hardpoint, `[2..n]` generator hardpoints
shield_link.meaning: Links a shield to the hardpoints of its generators; repeated keys **append**. Each line receives the next link id, counting up from 0xfff0. Parameters from `[2]` on are collected until the first empty one.
